chunks: Ali b. Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us from Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Rawyani from Abd al-Azim b. Abd al-Husni from Sulayman b. Ja'far al-Ja'fari. He said: I heard Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) say: My father narrated to me from his father from the Master of Worshippers Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them). He said:

Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) passed by a man who was speaking superfluously. So, he stopped by him, and then said: Surely, you are dictating a letter to your Lord through your two guardian angels. So, speak about what concerns you, and leave that which does not concern you.

key_terms.حافظيك: Your two guardians — the two recording angels who document every deed and word
key_terms.فضول الكلام: Superfluous speech — idle talk that serves no beneficial purpose
key_terms.كتابا إلى ربك: A letter to your Lord — the record presented on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about speaking too much and idle talk?
ai.summary: This ethical teaching, transmitted through a chain of Imams from Husayn to Ali, recounts how Imam Ali stopped by a man speaking excessively and warned him that his guardian angels are recording a letter to his Lord from every word he utters. The teaching urges speaking only about what matters and leaving aside idle talk. It was delivered as a public admonition, reflecting the Islamic principle that every spoken word is documented by the recording angels.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad al-Daqqaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us from `Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Rawyani from `Abd al-`Athim b. `Abd al-Husni from Sulayman b. Ja`far al-Ja`fari. He said: I heard Musa b. Ja`far (as) say: My father narrated to me from his father from the Master of Worshipers `Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as).  He said:

Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) passed by a man who was speaking superfluously. So, he stopped by him, and then said: Surely, you are dictating a letter to your Lord through your two guardian [angels]. So, speak about what concerns you, and leave that which does not concern you.
